narrative: The live LiteLLM exploitation sharpens the premise that unauthenticated remote MCP surfaces are the core failure. Two unauthenticated test endpoints accept a full server config and spawn it on the proxy host, yielding remote code execution with no login or API key. CISA's KEV listing and the authenticate-every-caller remediation turn the optional-auth gap into an actively-exploited one.
remaining_gap: No spec-body movement yet; the pressure is exploitation and federal advisory, not a published MCP revision requiring remote-server authentication.
